blocks.title: Phase
blocks.text: Angle θ = ωt, jo S.H.M karte point ka displacement x aur us ki motion ki direction (simt) dono batata hai, phase kehlata hai.

Phase woh quantity hai jo batati hai ke oscillator is waqt kis state of motion (halat) mein hai: kahan hai aur kis taraf ja raha hai. Circle mein ghoomti body ki diameter par projection S.H.M karti hai aur us ka displacement yeh hai:

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ne Eq. (14.17) ko x = x₀cos(ωt + 180°) chhapa hai. θ = ωt hai, is liye sahi x = x₀cos ωt hai; yahi Fig. 14.8 (a) (φ = 0) ka graph hai. x₀cos(ωt + 180°) to φ = 180° wala case hai (Fig. 14.8 (c)).
Yahan x instantaneous displacement, x₀ maximum displacement (amplitude) aur ω angular velocity hai; is ka graph Fig. 14.8 (a) mein hai. Is equation ki aam (general) shakal yeh hai:

Waqt ke saath badalne wali quantity (ωt + φ) motion ka phase hai; yeh kisi bhi waqt motion ki state (halat) batati hai. Constant φ ko phase constant (ya phase angle) kehte hain. φ ki value is par depend karti hai ke t = 0 par particle ka displacement aur velocity kya thi, yani motion kahan se shuru hui.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ke is paragraph mein do jagah φ ka nishaan chhapne se reh gaya hai ('The constant is called...', 'The value of the depends on φ...'). Sahi jumle yeh hain: constant φ phase constant hai, aur φ ki value t = 0 par displacement aur velocity par depend karti hai.
φ do oscillators ki states (halaton) ke darmiyan phase difference (phase ka farq) bhi batata hai. Ab x aur t ke graph se samajhte hain.
Agar φ = 0° ho to Eq. (14.18) yeh banti hai:

t = 0, T/4, T/2, 3T/4, T rakh kar Fig. 14.8 (a) ka graph milta hai. Is se pata chalta hai: t = 0, T/2 aur T par (θ = 0, π aur 2π) point extreme positions par hai, aur t = T/4 aur 3T/4 par (θ = π/2 aur 3π/2) mean position par.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ne yahan 'θ = 0, π and 2' chhapa hai; π reh gaya hai. Sahi θ = 0, π aur 2π hai.

blocks.alt: Aik period T mein displacement aur waqt ka graph; T/4, T/2, 3T/4 aur T likhe hain, xo aur -xo par dashed lines. Curve +xo se shuru, T/4 par zero, T/2 par -xo, 3T/4 par zero aur T par wapas +xo.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Is paragraph mein bhi kitab ne 'π and 2' (sahi 2π) aur 'θ = /2' (sahi θ = π/2) chhapa hai; π ka nishaan reh gaya hai.

t = 0, T/4, T/2, 3T/4, T rakh kar Fig. 14.8 (c) ka graph milta hai: yeh graph (a) ka bilkul ulta hai.

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: Teenon graph dekhein: amplitude aur period ek jaise hain, sirf shuru ki jagah alag hai. (a) +x₀ se, (b) zero se neeche ki taraf, aur (c) −x₀ se shuru hota hai. (a) aur (c) hamesha O ke ulti taraf hain: yeh out of phase hain.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ne Fig. 14.8 (b) ke neeche caption 'φ = 0°' aur (c) ke neeche 'φ = 90°' chhapa hai, aur (c) mein neeche wale nishaan par −x₀ ki jagah 'x₀' likha hai. Text ke mutabiq (b) φ = 90° aur (c) φ = 180° hai; khaake isi ke mutabiq hain.
Yaad rakhein:
Jab do jhoolne wale systems ka phase difference 180° ho to woh out of phase (ulte qadam) jhoolte hain: ek daen kinare par ho to doosra baen kinare par.
Jab phase difference 0° ya 360° ho to woh in phase (ek saath, qadam mila kar) jhoolte hain.

blocks.title: Example 14.4
blocks.problem: 0.5 kg mass 200 N m⁻¹ spring constant wale spring se bandha hai. Mass ko equilibrium se 0.2 m hata kar rest se chhora jata hai. S.H.M assume (farz) kar ke nikalein: (a) t = 0.5 s par displacement (b) t = 0.5 s par velocity (c) t = 0.5 s par acceleration.
steps: Diya gaya: m = 0.5 kg, k = 200 N m⁻¹, amplitude x₀ = 0.2 m. Mass extreme position se chhora gaya, is liye x = x₀cos(ωt).
ωt = 20 × 0.5 = 10 rad. Dhyan dein: 10 radian (taqreeban 573°) third quadrant mein hai, is liye cos(10) = −0.839 aur sin(10) = −0.544 (calculator ko radian mode mein rakhein).
(a) x = x₀cos(ωt) = 0.2 × (−0.839) = −0.168 m (mass O ki doosri taraf hai)
blocks.answer: x = −0.168 m, v = +2.176 m s⁻¹, a = +67.12 m s⁻² (magnitudes kitab jaisi, signs sahi kiye gaye).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ne cos(10) = +0.839 aur sin(10) = +0.544 liye hain aur x = 0.168 m, v = 2.176 m s⁻¹ aur a = −67.12 m s⁻² diye hain. 10 radian ke liye cos aur sin dono negative (manfi) hain, is liye sahi x = −0.168 m aur a = +67.12 m s⁻² hai; velocity direction ke saath v = −x₀ω sin(ωt) = +2.176 m s⁻¹ hai. Hissa (c) mein kitab ne 't = 0.05 s' bhi chhapa hai, jo t = 0.5 s hona chahiye.

blocks.prompt: Do ek jaise pendulum is tarah jhoolte hain ke jab ek daen kinare par ho to doosra baen kinare par hota hai. Un ka phase difference kya hai?
blocks.explanation: 180° (π radian): woh out of phase hain.

blocks.text: Short summary (mukhtasar khulasa)

items: Phase (ωt + φ) batata hai ke oscillator kahan hai aur kis taraf ja raha hai; φ phase constant hai.
x = x₀cos(ωt + φ): φ = 0 par +x₀ se, φ = 90° par mean position se, φ = 180° par −x₀ se shuru.
Phase difference 0° ya 360°: in phase; 180°: out of phase.
